title: 90s themes
text: theme_gameboy() uses four shades green original Game Boy screen pixel font Press Start 2P, ships fmggp2. simulate starter chosen 300 Pokémon Red Blue players.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(1998) pokemon_starters <- data.frame(   starter = sample(c("Bulbasaur", "Charmander", "Squirtle"),     size = 300, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.30, 0.42, 0.28)) ) ggplot(pokemon_starters, aes(x = starter, fill = starter)) +   geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Pokemon Red and Blue (simulated)",        subtitle = "Starter chosen by 300 players",        x = "Starter", y = "Count") +   theme_gameboy(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_oksoda() uses gray comic book cans Coca-Cola sold 1993 1995: brushed silver, black ink, OK red bars title, slate brick accents, Courier New title. simulate one day sales 300 test market stores normal distribution.  Image: TeemPlayer, Wikimedia Commons, CC -SA 3.0.
code: set.seed(1014) ok_soda_sales <- data.frame(   cans = round(rnorm(n = 300, mean = 45, sd = 12)) ) ggplot(ok_soda_sales, aes(x = cans)) +   geom_histogram(bins = 30) +   labs(title = "OK Soda", caption = "Simulated data",        subtitle = "Cans sold per store in one day",        x = "Cans sold") +   theme_oksoda(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_talkboy() uses Deluxe Talkboy Home Alone 2 sitting walnut table: silver panel, button blue marks, Brush Script title. simulate length 300 recorded messages right skewed gamma distribution.  Image: Y2kcrazyjoker4, Wikimedia Commons, CC -SA 4.0.
code: set.seed(1999) talkboy_clips <- data.frame(   seconds = round(rgamma(n = 300, shape = 4, rate = 0.5), 1) ) ggplot(talkboy_clips, aes(x = seconds)) +   geom_freqpoly(bins = 30) +   labs(title = "Talkboy", caption = "Simulated data",        subtitle = "Length of 300 recorded messages",        x = "Message length (seconds)") +   theme_talkboy(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_blockbuster() uses Blockbuster Video blue yellow. simulate weekly rentals 60 households Poisson distribution.  Image: Jon Konrath Oakland, USA, Wikimedia Commons, CC 2.0.
code: set.seed(1993) blockbuster_rentals <- data.frame(rentals = rpois(n = 60, lambda = 3)) ggplot(blockbuster_rentals, aes(x = rentals)) +   geom_dotplot(binwidth = 1, dotsize = 0.3) +   labs(title = "Blockbuster Video (simulated)",        x = "Number of rentals") +   theme_blockbuster(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_crystalpepsi() uses clear bottle label: cream background, navy frame, Pepsi red navy marks, Futura title. simulate ages 400 people 1992 mall taste test mix kids parents.  Image: Mike Mozart, Wikimedia Commons, CC 2.0.
code: set.seed(1998) kid <- runif(400) < 0.65 tasters <- data.frame(group = ifelse(kid, "Kid", "Parent"),   age = round(ifelse(kid, rnorm(400, 11, 2.5), rnorm(400, 37, 6)))) ggplot(tasters, aes(x = age, fill = group)) +   geom_density(alpha = 2/3) +   labs(title = "Crystal Pepsi", caption = "Simulated data",        x = "Age (years)", fill = NULL) +   theme_crystalpepsi(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_beanie() uses Ty heart tag red blanket teal fur colors Beanie. simulate 300 resale prices log normal distribution.  Image: “Beanie Baby” ajay_suresh, CC 2.0.
code: set.seed(1996) beanie_prices <- data.frame(price = rlnorm(n = 300, meanlog = log(15), sdlog = 0.8)) ggplot(beanie_prices, aes(x = "", y = price)) +   geom_violin() +   labs(title = "Beanie Babies resale prices (simulated)",        x = NULL, y = "Price (USD)") +   theme_beanie(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_n64() uses controller gray four logo colors. simulate 200 Mario Kart 64 lap times heavy tailed t distribution.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(64) mario_kart_laps <- data.frame(seconds = 45 + 2 * rt(n = 200, df = 3)) ggplot(mario_kart_laps, aes(x = "", y = seconds)) +   geom_boxplot() +   labs(title = "Mario Kart 64 (simulated)",        x = NULL, y = "Lap time (seconds)") +   theme_n64(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_jurassic() uses Jurassic Park Post Office souvenir sheet: black, logo red, stamp yellow, sunset orange. simulate total weight dinosaurs paddock.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, CC0.
code: set.seed(1993) jp_paddocks <- data.frame(species = c("Brachiosaurus", "Triceratops", "Tyrannosaurus"),   total_tons = c(sum(rnorm(3, 40, 5)), sum(rnorm(5, 9, 1.2)), sum(rnorm(2, 8, 1)))) ggplot(jp_paddocks, aes(x = species, y = total_tons, fill = species)) +   geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Jurassic Park (simulated)", x = "Paddock", y = "Total weight (tons)") +   theme_jurassic(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_happymeal() uses red yellow Happy Meal box. simulate average daily Happy Meal sales four toy promotions.  Image: Newtown grafitti Sydney, Australia, Wikimedia Commons, CC 2.0.
code: set.seed(1997) happy_meals <- data.frame(promotion = c("Teenie Beanie Babies", "Furby", "Hot Wheels", "Inspector Gadget"),   avg_sold = sapply(c(420, 310, 220, 180), function(l) mean(rpois(28, l)))) ggplot(happy_meals, aes(x = promotion, y = avg_sold, fill = promotion)) +   geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Happy Meals (simulated)", x = "Toy promotion", y = "Average sold per day") +   theme_happymeal(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_friends() uses Monica’s apartment: purple walls, cream sofa, latte frame, poppy red, navy, wood, rust, rose marks. simulate viewers per episode three seasons.  Image: “Monica’s Apartment, Friends” Rob Young, CC 2.0.
code: set.seed(1994) friends_episodes <- data.frame(season = rep(c("Season 1", "Season 3", "Season 5"), each = 24)) friends_episodes$viewers_m <- round(rnorm(72, rep(c(22, 27, 24), each = 24), 2.5)) ggplot(friends_episodes, aes(x = viewers_m, fill = season)) +   geom_bar() +   labs(title = "Friends (simulated)", x = "Viewers (millions)", y = "Episodes", fill = "Season") +   theme_friends(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_freshprince() uses logo: graffiti greens pink glow, continuous fill runs teal lime. simulate often Carlton dance shows season.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(1990) fp <- expand.grid(season = 1:6, gag = c("Will flirts", "Carlton dance")) fp$occurrences <- rbinom(12, 24, ifelse(fp$gag == "Will flirts", 0.9, plogis(-2.2 + 0.5 * (fp$season - 3.5)))) ggplot(fp, aes(x = season, y = gag, fill = occurrences)) +   geom_tile() +   labs(title = "Fresh Prince (simulated)", x = "Season", y = NULL, fill = "Episodes") +   theme_freshprince(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_pogs() uses cardboard background red, sky blue, yellow, teal, purple, rust milk cap prints. simulate collection 100 Pogs.  Image: “Remember Pogs?” MTSOfan, CC -NC-SA 2.0.
code: set.seed(1993) pogs <- data.frame(type = sample(c("Milk caps", "Printed pogs", "Holographic", "Slammers"),   100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.45, 0.30, 0.15, 0.10))) ggplot(pogs, aes(x = type, fill = type)) +   geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(title = "A Pogs collection (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Pieces") +   theme_pogs(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_walkman() uses Sports Walkman: sports yellow body, blue buttons, charcoal display, orange SPORTS label. simulate median battery life three models two battery types.  Image: Itsramon, Wikimedia Commons, CC -SA 3.0.
code: set.seed(1979) walkman <- data.frame(model = rep(c("WM-2", "WM-F45 Sports", "WM-EX194 Mega Bass"), times = 2),   battery = rep(c("Alkaline", "Rechargeable"), each = 3), hours = c(10, 16, 22, 7, 12, 17) + rnorm(6, 0, 0.5)) ggplot(walkman, aes(x = hours, y = model)) +   geom_line(aes(group = model)) +   geom_point(aes(color = battery), size = 3) +   labs(title = "Sony Walkman (simulated)", x = "Median battery life (hours)", y = NULL, color = "Battery") +   theme_walkman(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_orbitz() uses bottle Orbitz, 1997 drink floating gel balls: black background, gold frame, gold magenta marks, Marker Felt title. compare share kids buying Orbitz Surge week Orbitz arrived.  Image: Jesse! S?, Wikimedia Commons, CC 2.0.
code: p_surge <- 0.8 * plogis(-2 + 0.6 * (0:6)) drinks <- data.frame(week = factor(rep(1:7, 2)),   choice = factor(rep(c("Surge", "Orbitz"), each = 7), levels = c("Surge", "Orbitz")),   share = c(p_surge, -(0.8 - p_surge))) ggplot(drinks, aes(x = week, y = share, fill = choice)) +   geom_col(width = 0.5) +   labs(title = "Orbitz vs. Surge", caption = "Simulated data",        x = "Week", y = "Share of kids", fill = NULL) +   theme_orbitz(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_netscape(): Netscape Navigator logo, night sky teal, aurora green, sea glass, deep teal marks, Times New Roman title.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, CC0.
code: set.seed(1996) modem <- sample(c("14.4k", "28.8k", "56k"), 600, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.25, 0.45, 0.30)) speeds <- data.frame(modem = modem,   kbps = rnorm(600, c(`14.4k` = 13, `28.8k` = 26, `56k` = 44)[modem], c(`14.4k` = 1.2, `28.8k` = 2.5, `56k` = 5)[modem])) ggplot(speeds, aes(x = kbps, after_stat(count), fill = modem)) +   geom_density(position = "fill") +   labs(title = "Dial up speeds (simulated)", x = "Speed (kbps)", fill = "Modem") +   theme_netscape(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_titanic(): Vallejo Titanic Colors paint set (black, yellow, canvas, anti-fouling red, faded yellow, stone, wood deck) Big Caslon title.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(1997) fans <- data.frame(age_group = sample(c("Teen", "Adult"), 300, replace = TRUE),   viewings = sample(c("Once", "Twice", "3+ times"), 300, replace = TRUE)) ggplot(fans, aes(x = age_group, fill = viewings)) +   geom_bar(position = "fill") +   labs(title = "Titanic (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Share", fill = "Viewings") +   theme_titanic(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_koosh() uses tri color Koosh ball: white background, orange frame, orange, purple, black marks, Arial Rounded title. simulate styles 200 Koosh balls sold toy store.  Image: Evan-Amos, Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(1993) koosh_balls <- data.frame(style = factor(sample(c("Tri color", "Rainbow", "Neon", "Glow"),   200, replace = TRUE, prob = c(1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8)),   levels = c("Tri color", "Rainbow", "Neon", "Glow"))) ggplot(koosh_balls, aes(x = style, fill = style)) +   geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Koosh balls", caption = "Simulated data", x = NULL, y = "Sold") +   theme_koosh(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_toysrus(): Toys”R”Us white blue multicolored logo letters marks Phosphate title.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(1999) toys <- data.frame(toy = c("Furby", "Beanie Babies", "Game Boy Color", "Nintendo 64"),   units = rpois(4, c(1800, 2400, 1200, 1000))) ggplot(toys, aes(x = toy, y = units, fill = toy)) +   geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Toys\"R\"Us 1998 (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Units sold") +   theme_toysrus(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_tamagotchi(): lilac egg shell gray green LCD screen. simulate Tamagotchi lifespans Weibull distribution.  Image: Dex Vintage, Wikimedia Commons, CC 3.0.
code: set.seed(1997) pets <- data.frame(care = rep(c("Neglected", "Pampered"), each = 150)) pets$days <- rweibull(300, shape = 2.2, scale = ifelse(pets$care == "Neglected", 6, 21)) ggplot(pets, aes(x = days, fill = care)) +   geom_histogram(alpha = 2/3, position = "identity", bins = 40) +   labs(title = "Tamagotchi lifespans (simulated)", x = "Days", fill = "Care") +   theme_tamagotchi(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_supersoaker(): neon orange plastic, water blue, neon green. simulate Super Soaker ranges two models.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, CC -SA 3.0.
code: set.seed(1990) shots <- data.frame(model = rep(c("SS 50", "CPS 2000"), each = 200)) shots$feet <- rnorm(400, ifelse(shots$model == "SS 50", 25, 45), ifelse(shots$model == "SS 50", 3, 5.4)) ggplot(shots, aes(x = feet, color = model)) +   geom_freqpoly(binwidth = 2, linewidth = 1) +   labs(title = "Super Soaker range (simulated)", x = "Range (feet)", color = "Model") +   theme_supersoaker(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_goosebumps(): slime green logo purple covers Goosebumps books black, Trattatello title. simulate Goosebumps books read two grades.
code: set.seed(1992) readers <- data.frame(grade = rep(c("3rd grade", "5th grade"), each = 40)) readers$books <- rpois(80, ifelse(readers$grade == "3rd grade", 3, 9)) ggplot(readers, aes(x = books, fill = grade)) +   geom_dotplot(method = "histodot", binwidth = 1, stackgroups = TRUE, binpositions = "all") +   labs(title = "Goosebumps (simulated)", x = "Books read", fill = "Grade") +   theme_goosebumps(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_tetris(): black well tetromino block colors. simulate lines cleared negative binomial distribution.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(1989) games <- data.frame(player = rep(c("Casual", "Expert"), each = 80)) games$lines <- rnbinom(160, size = 5, mu = ifelse(games$player == "Casual", 25, 120)) ggplot(games, aes(x = player, y = lines, color = player)) +   geom_jitter(width = 0.2, show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Tetris (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Lines cleared") +   theme_tetris(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_furby(): 1998 Furby’s teal fur, gray belly, beak yellow, pink. simulate Furby chatter two languages.  Image: “Furby” Amanda (blamethecrane), CC -ND 2.0.
code: set.seed(1998) chatter <- data.frame(language = rep(c("Furbish", "English"), times = c(180, 120))) chatter$words <- rnorm(300, ifelse(chatter$language == "Furbish", 45, 30), ifelse(chatter$language == "Furbish", 8, 10)) ggplot(chatter, aes(x = words, after_stat(count), fill = language)) +   geom_density(alpha = 1/2) +   labs(title = "Furby chatter (simulated)", x = "Words per hour", fill = "Language") +   theme_furby(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_squeezit() uses Squeezit bottles standing gravel: gravel background, red frame title, red, orange, green, pink, blue, gold marks, Skia title. simulate seconds took squeeze three flavors gamma distribution.  Image: ZolHaj, Wikimedia Commons, CC -SA 4.0.
code: set.seed(1998) bottles <- data.frame(flavor = factor(rep(c("Cherry", "Orange", "Green punch"), each = 60),   levels = c("Cherry", "Orange", "Green punch"))) bottles$seconds <- rgamma(180, shape = 2.5,   scale = c(Cherry = 12, Orange = 18, `Green punch` = 22)[as.character(bottles$flavor)] / 2.5) ggplot(bottles, aes(x = seconds, fill = flavor)) +   geom_density(alpha = 2/3) +   labs(title = "Squeezit", caption = "Simulated data",        x = "Seconds to finish", fill = "Flavor") +   theme_squeezit(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_oregontrail(): Oregon Trail running Apple II emulator, gray window frame, black screen, three shades phosphor green. simulate days reach Oregon log normal distribution.  Image: Pug Father, Flickr, CC 2.0.
code: set.seed(1985) trips <- data.frame(profession = rep(c("Banker", "Carpenter", "Farmer"), each = 100)) trips$days <- rlnorm(300, log(c(Banker = 140, Carpenter = 155, Farmer = 170)[trips$profession]), 0.2) ggplot(trips, aes(x = profession, y = days, fill = profession)) +   geom_boxplot(alpha = 2/3, show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(title = "The Oregon Trail (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Days") +   theme_oregontrail(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_aim(): sign window’s gray, AOL blue, sky blue, yellow running man. simulate buddy list sizes different shapes.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(1997) buddies <- data.frame(school = rep(c("Middle school", "College"), each = 150)) buddies$n <- ifelse(buddies$school == "Middle school", rpois(300, 20), ifelse(runif(300) < 0.7, rnorm(300, 60, 10), rnorm(300, 150, 20))) ggplot(buddies, aes(x = school, y = n, fill = school)) +   geom_violin(alpha = 2/3, show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(title = "AIM buddy lists (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Buddies") +   theme_aim(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_rzone() uses Tiger’s 1995 R-Zone headset: black plastic, red frame title, red LCD, purple, pink marks, pale blue visor text, Arial Narrow title. simulate seconds 100 players needed clear first level two tries.  Image: Evan-Amos, Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(1993) tries <- data.frame(try = rep(c("First", "Second"), each = 100)) tries$seconds <- rlnorm(200, log(ifelse(tries$try == "First", 40, 20)), 0.5) ggplot(tries, aes(x = seconds, y = try, fill = try)) +   geom_boxplot(width = 0.3, show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Tiger R-Zone", caption = "Simulated data",        x = "Seconds to clear the first level", y = NULL) +   theme_rzone(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_batman() comes three versions. default, version = "movie", uses Batman (1989) palette: black, gold, orange, steel. simulate bat signal sightings week.  Image: Mbrickn, Wikimedia Commons, CC -SA 4.0.  version = "classic" uses 1966 TV series palette: gray, blue, yellow, black, cream.   version = "darknight" uses Dark Knight palette: yellow, olive, charcoal, navy, slate.
code: set.seed(1989) signals <- data.frame(night = factor(c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"), levels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")), sightings = rpois(7, 12)) ggplot(signals, aes(x = night, y = sightings)) +   geom_col() +   labs(title = "Bat signal sightings (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Sightings") +   theme_batman(base_size = 13) ggplot(signals, aes(x = night, y = sightings)) +   geom_col() +   labs(title = "Bat signal sightings (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Sightings") +   theme_batman(base_size = 13, version = "classic") ggplot(signals, aes(x = night, y = sightings)) +   geom_col() +   labs(title = "Bat signal sightings (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Sightings") +   theme_batman(base_size = 13, version = "darknight")

title: 90s themes
text: theme_snick(): Nickelodeon orange slime green night purple sky. simulate 20 weeks ratings three nights.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(1992) nights <- expand.grid(week = 1:20, night = c("Fri", "Sat", "Sun")) nights$rating <- c(Fri = 2.8, Sat = 4.2, Sun = 3.0)[as.character(nights$night)] + rnorm(60, 0, 0.3) ggplot(nights, aes(x = week, y = rating, color = night)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   labs(title = "SNICK ratings (simulated)", x = "Week", y = "Rating", color = NULL) +   theme_snick(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_boyband(): midnight navy, chrome, frosted tip colors. simulate week radio spins four bands.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(1999) spins <- data.frame(band = c("Backstreet Boys", "*NSYNC", "98 Degrees", "LFO")) spins$spins <- rpois(4, c(420, 380, 330, 300)) ggplot(spins, aes(x = band, y = spins, fill = band)) +   geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Boy band spins (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Spins") +   theme_boyband(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_savedbythebell(): logo’s sky blue, pink, yellow, orange black. simulate fall spring quiz averages three students.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: set.seed(1989) grades <- data.frame(student = rep(c("Zack", "Kelly", "Screech"), 2),                      semester = rep(c("Fall", "Spring"), each = 3)) grades$score <- c(70, 82, 93, 80, 82, 95) + rnorm(6, 0, 2) ggplot(grades, aes(x = semester, y = score, group = student, color = student)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 2) +   geom_point(size = 4) +   labs(title = "Bayside quizzes (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Average score", color = NULL) +   theme_savedbythebell(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_hypercolor(): heat changing magenta, orange, purple, blue. simulate monthly sales two fads.  Image: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
code: months <- seq(1990, 1995, by = 1 / 12) fads <- data.frame(month = rep(months, 2),                    fad = rep(c("Hypercolor", "Slap bracelets"), each = length(months))) fads$sales <- ifelse(fads$fad == "Hypercolor",                      4000 * dnorm(fads$month, 1991.5, 0.6),                      3000 * dnorm(fads$month, 1990.8, 0.4)) / 12 ggplot(fads, aes(x = month, y = sales, fill = fad)) +   geom_area(alpha = 0.8) +   labs(title = "90s fads (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Sales (thousands)", fill = NULL) +   theme_hypercolor(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_y2k(): LED red, terminal amber green black. show 300 households prepared Y2K across three surveys.  Image: Bug de l’2000, Wikimedia Commons, CC -SA 3.0.
code: prep <- data.frame(   survey = factor(rep(c("Jan", "Jul", "Dec"), each = 3), levels = c("Jan", "Jul", "Dec")),   level = factor(rep(c("Not worried", "Some supplies", "Bunker ready"), 3),                  levels = c("Not worried", "Some supplies", "Bunker ready")),   households = c(163, 100, 37, 124, 119, 57, 108, 117, 75)) ggplot(prep, aes(x = survey, y = households, fill = level)) +   geom_col() +   labs(title = "Y2K prep (simulated)", x = NULL, y = "Households", fill = NULL) +   theme_y2k(base_size = 13)

title: 90s themes
text: theme_gushers() uses pile Fruit Gushers white plate: red frame title, red, green, teal, orange, pink marks, Chalkboard title. simulate fruit snack trades one lunch table Gushers arrived 1991.  Image: Thomson200, Wikimedia Commons, CC0.
